title: AeroFlux Systems Onboarding Brief & Ops Handoff
summary: Kickoff/hand-off focused on network access for a VPC-based Private deployment, initial traffic patterns, SSO + SCIM onboarding, and a short pilot plan for a throughput-heavy inference use case. Customer has an aggressive Q3 pilot target and requested security docs and a staging topology by Friday. Some audio glitches, transcription contains minor mis-hears.
topics: Pilot scope (throughput test for recommendation service)
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We're running on a 45 minute block, we'll cover ops handoff and the immediate next steps.
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hey, thanks Priya. We got your invite, and yep, excited to get this moving. Our Q3 pilot window is kind of non-negotiable.
[00:18] Tom Nguyen: Quick intro — I'm Tom, I'll be the SE partnering on the infra bits and the perf tests.
[00:24] Daniel Park: Daniel here. We'll be the infra owners, we run in AWS in a single-account VPC today, some services in a private subnet behind NAT.
[00:33] Priya Shah: Great context. Victor, you were going to lead security?
[00:37] Victor Hsu: Yeah, I'll be looking at KMS, key lifecycle, and the audit log retention. We need to understand what logs Redwood exposes, retention periods, and whether we can ingest to our SIEM.
[00:47] Elena Park: We have a standard Audit Logs export to S3 option and CloudTrail-friendly payloads, and we can push events to a customer-owned bucket —
[00:55] Victor Hsu: Right, but we need guarantees for retention and a way to query separately for per-tenant traces.
[01:03] Tom Nguyen: For Private deployments we support export of inference traces and per-token billing logs. Retention by default is 30 days in the console, longer retention is an add-on. We can open a ticket to layer in the longer retention and delivery to your S3.
[01:15] Daniel Park: Ok, and what about KMS? Do you require we use your KMS or can we bring our own?
[01:21] Priya Shah: You're able to BYOK via customer KMS in your cloud; we integrate with customer-managed keys for data at rest.
[01:28] Maya Solis: On the pilot side, the model we'll use is the recommendation reranker — high qps, short sequence length. We want to validate tail latency at 95th and 99th pct.
[01:38] Tom Nguyen: That's helpful — so perf tests will focus on concurrency and tail. We'll propose a burst/capacity config and a steady-state throughput target.
[01:46] Lena Ortiz: Network wise — we want minimal blast radius. What's the minimal set of ports and subnets to allow?
[01:52] Tom Nguyen: Minimal is egress to Redwood EIP pool on 443 and an inbound for a management SSH jumpbox if you want remote debug, but we can do ephemeral logs through the control plane. We'll send a one-pager.
[02:05] Daniel Park: Is peering better than PrivateLink for us? We're in a restricted environment with some cross-account rules.
[02:11] Elena Park: PrivateLink is supported but has throughput implications and costs; peering is straightforward if you allow routing, but PrivateLink removes route table exposure.
[02:20] Victor Hsu: Cost is less of a concern than isolation. We prefer PrivateLink if possible.
[02:25] Tom Nguyen: Noted. For heavy throughput pilots PrivateLink can saturate if not sized properly; we'll include recommendations and projected egress costs.
[02:33] Lena Ortiz: On identity, we need SSO with SCIM provisioning. Outline the steps?
[02:38] Priya Shah: We'll share our SAML metadata and support SSO + SCIM for group sync. Typical flow: exchange metadata, validate in staging, then do SCIM sync for the pilot users.
[02:48] Maya Solis: Who sets up the initial test users?
[02:50] Elena Park: The customer creates a test group and we trigger a SCIM push; we can also do manual invites for three pilot users to speed up.
[02:58] Daniel Park: We will need RBAC mappings; can we map to our internal AD groups?
[03:03] Tom Nguyen: Yes, you can map groups to roles. We'll send the role mapping template.
[03:08] Priya Shah: Timeline check — pilot kickoff ideally next Monday (2025-06-16). Is that feasible?
[03:14] Lena Ortiz: tight but doable if we get staging topology and creds by Friday.
[03:18] Victor Hsu: We'll need security docs (SOC2, pen test results, configuration hardening guide) to run the internal approvals.
[03:25] Priya Shah: I'll attach the latest SOC2 summary and the infra hardening checklist. Tom will send the staging topology.
[03:31] Tom Nguyen: I'll also attach a sample perf harness and the instrumentation hooks for KV cache metrics — excuse me, KV cache we use to check warm start latencies.
[03:41] Lena Ortiz: Can you also clarify the model pinning behavior during a rollout? We want deterministic versioning for the duration of the pilot.
[03:48] Elena Park: You can pin model version and we support canary rollouts; for pilots we recommend pinning to a specific model hash for the timeframe.
[03:56] Maya Solis: Any blockers on billing? We need a sandbox billing token for the QA team.
[04:01] Priya Shah: We'll issue a trial billing token for the pilot stage and provide cost estimates for the projected QPS.
[04:08] Daniel Park: Ok. A few open items — network diagram, SAML metadata, SOC2, KMS BYOK steps, pilot perf target spreadsheet.
[04:16] Priya Shah: We'll consolidate into a single Slack thread and the shared Confluence page.
[04:20] Tom Nguyen: I'll also schedule the perf run with your infra window and do a dry run in staging.
[04:25] Victor Hsu: Side note — do you provide granular token-level logs we can consume into Splunk?
[04:30] Tom Nguyen: Yes, logs can be exported as newline-delimited JSON to your S3 and you can ingest to Splunk. There might be minimal PII redaction by default; we can flag any extra redaction requirements.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: That helps. Any competitors or alternatives we should be aware of from Redwood's side?
[04:44] Priya Shah: Customers sometimes evaluate bedrock-style managed endpoints (AWS), Databricks model serving, and in-house Triton stacks. We'll share a short comparison doc focused on latency and cost.
[04:55] Maya Solis: Great.
[04:57] Priya Shah: Ok quick recap — deliverables by Friday: staging topology, SAML metadata exchange, SOC2 summary, pilot perf spreadsheet, and role mapping template. Pilot kickoff targeted Monday 6/16.
[05:12] Daniel Park: Good, we will review and escalate internally.
[05:16] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, everyone.
[05:19] Priya Shah: Thank you, we'll follow up in the thread.
[05:22] (call ends)

Note: occasional audio drop at 00:34-00:36, some names slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., Elena/Elaina), timestamps approximate based on auto-timestamping.
